04

Stay Protected

Short lessons for people, families, and small businesses.

1. Pause before you click

Unexpected links, urgent deadlines, gift cards, crypto, or login codes are warning signs. Open the official site yourself instead.

2. Verify the person

Call back using a number you find independently. Do not trust a number, QR code, or link in the unexpected message.

3. Protect your accounts

Use a different password for every account and turn on multi-factor authentication. Never share a one-time login code.

4. If you clicked or paid

Change the password, contact your bank or card company, report the incident, and tell coworkers or family quickly.

05

I clicked, paid, or shared a code

Act quickly. This checklist is private and does not report anything for you.

1. Secure your account

Change the affected password from a trusted device. Turn on multi-factor authentication and sign out of other sessions.

2. Protect your money

Call your bank or card company using the number on its official website or the back of your card. Ask them to stop or review the transaction.

3. Report and tell others

Save screenshots. Report the scam to the service involved and warn your workplace or family so no one else uses the same link.
